headline: EU regulatory update: Green claims withdrawal, Ecodesign repairability, and battery compliance
summary: Reports indicate the European Commission plans to scrap the Green Claims Directive. Meanwhile, new EU consultations on Ecodesign repairability focus on product durability. For your Chinese supply base, compliance with the EU Battery Regulation is advancing, and revised ESRS standards enter force ahead of your FY2027 CSRD reporting scope.

items.title: Commission reported to withdraw proposed Green Claims Directive
items.what: Media reports indicate the European Commission intends to withdraw the Green Claims Directive proposal.
items.meaning: While specific green claims substantiation rules are dropped, general anti-greenwashing rules under the Empowering Consumers Directive remain in force for tool packaging and marketing.
items.action: Review product packaging and marketing claims against existing EU consumer protection standards.

sources.title: EU Commission Abandons Plans For The Green Claims Directive
Commission confirms plans to scrap Green Claims Directive

items.title: EU opens consultation on Ecodesign repairability rules
items.what: The EU has launched a consultation regarding new repairability and durability requirements under Ecodesign rules.
items.meaning: Future rules will mandate easier disassembly, spare part access, and repair information for your power tools and garden equipment manufactured in China.
items.action: Assess current tool designs and spare part availability with Chinese OEM suppliers.

sources.title: Fix it, don't bin it: the EU consults on Ecodesign repairability requirements

items.title: Chinese battery supplier obtains EU Battery Regulation certification
items.what: TWS Technology attained TÜV Rheinland conformity certification under the EU Battery Regulation.
items.meaning: Demonstrates that Chinese battery platform suppliers are actively obtaining EU conformity certifications, a critical step before mandatory battery passport rules take effect.
items.action: Verify EU Battery Regulation readiness and certification roadmaps with your battery pack suppliers.

sources.title: EU Battery Regulation: TWS Technology Attains TÜV Rheinland Conformity

items.title: Omnibus Reform analysis details updated CSRD obligations
items.what: Legal analysis details ESG reporting changes following the Omnibus Reform, as revised ESRS rules entered into force on 10 November 2026.
items.meaning: Confirms your CSRD reporting timeline starting in FY2027, requiring structured ESG data collection across your Chinese supply chain.
items.action: Ensure supplier sustainability data collection aligns with revised ESRS metrics for FY2027.

sources.title: ESG disclosure and corporate due diligence obligations under the Omnibus Reform
